Little bit explain

Certainly. "Biselining" refers to making small, undocumented changes to a requirement without
updating its formal documentation. This can affect the requirement's traceability, which is the ability
to track the development and testing of the requirement through various stages of a project.

When requirements are changed without proper documentation, it becomes difficult to trace back
how and why the requirement was altered. This can lead to confusion, misinterpretation, and
challenges in ensuring that the final product aligns with the original intention. Properly maintaining
traceability is important for understanding the rationale behind requirements and ensuring that the
final product meets the intended goals.

Time-boxing is used in severe deadline pressure. It is a use incremental strategy where tasks

Furthermore, there are predictable and unpredictable risks. Predictable risks can be

Risk Identification

It is the responsibility of the project manager to identify known and predictable risks.
These risks fall in the following categories of generic risks and product specific risks.
Generic risks are threats to every project whereas Product specific risks are specific to a
particular project. The question to be asked in this context is: what special characteristics
of this project may threaten your project plan? A useful technique in this regards is the
preparation of a risk item checklist. This list tries to ask and answer questions relevant to
each of the following topics for each software project:

   •   Product size
   •   Business impact
   •   Customer characteristics
   •   Process definition
   •   Development environment
   •   Technology to be built
   •   Staff size and experience

   •   Have top software and customer managers formally committed to support the

   •   Are requirements fully understood?
   •   Have customers been involved fully in requirement definition?

• Casual

Can we guarantee 100% risk free software development i.e. can we develop a software without risk by
following some software procedure? Comment it. 5 marks
Answer:- Click here for detail
Let’s be clear: there’s no such thing as risk free software. You can’t do anythingwithout taking some risk. But
what’s easy to overlook, is that not doing something is a risk, too.
Not fixing a bug runs the risk that its more serious than you thought; more prevalent than you thought; that it
could happen to an important customer, someone in the press, or a highly valued customer – with real revenue
risk. You run the risk that it collides with another, as yet unknown bug, potentially multiplying the pain.
